Mesoscale Discussion 1869
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0510 PM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

   Areas affected...Portions of the Carolinas

   Concerning...Severe potential...Watch unlikely 

   Valid 082210Z - 090015Z

   Probability of Watch Issuance...5 percent

   SUMMARY...Sporadic damaging winds will be possible for the next
   couple of hours across parts of South Carolina and western/central
   North Carolina. Watch issuance is not expected.

   DISCUSSION...Thunderstorms have been slowly intensifying along the
   Appalachians over the past 2-3 hours per regional radar imagery and
   lightning trends. More recently, much of this activity has exhibited
   strong outflow - a manifestation of the poor kinematic environment
   (also confirmed by regional VWPs). Furthermore, west/southwesterly
   mid-level flow is favoring storm motions along the zone of ascent,
   which is limiting southeastward propagation into a more deeply-mixed
   and buoyant air mass (characterized by 0-3 km lapse rates near 8
   C/km and around 1000 J/kg MLCAPE). 

   Nonetheless, some degree of storm propagation into the
   well-mixed/buoyant air is probable as outflows surge
   south/southeastward and collide. Convection developing within this
   regime will be capable of produce strong downbursts with embedded
   swaths of damaging winds (most likely 45-60 mph). Confidence in the
   coverage and/or duration of intense convection is very limited and
   precludes watch issuance, but a few instances of wind damage appear
   possible over the next couple of hours prior to the onset of
   nocturnal cooling after 00 UTC.

   ..Moore/Mosier.. 08/08/2026

   ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

Mesoscale Discussion 1867
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0453 PM CDT Sat Aug 08 2026

   Areas affected...portions of northern Kansas

   Concerning...Severe potential...Watch unlikely 

   Valid 082153Z - 082330Z

   Probability of Watch Issuance...20 percent

   SUMMARY...A couple instances of severe gusts or perhaps some hail
   may accompany any of the stronger storms that manage to sustain
   themselves through the remainder of the afternoon.

   DISCUSSION...A lone multicellular cluster has matured over northern
   KS in the past hour, likely driven by the intersection of a strongly
   heated/mixed boundary layer and weak surface convergence along a
   baroclinic boundary. A belt of 15-20 kt southerly low-level flow is
   in place across the Plains, overspread by 30+ kt 500 mb
   northwesterlies, resulting in 40+ kts of effective bulk shear over
   northern KS. The baroclinic boundary precedes the ongoing
   multicellular cluster, where surface dewpoints exceed 70 F, yielding
   over 3000 J/kg MLCAPE. Nonetheless, forcing for ascent is weak in
   this region, casting great uncertainty on the coverage and overall
   longevity of any severe threat. Current visible satellite does not
   suggest any imminent threat for additional convective development in
   the near term. Still, given adequate vertical wind shear and
   instability, a conditional threat for a few severe gusts and perhaps
   an instance of severe hail may accompany this multicellular cluster,
   assuming it persists along the baroclinic boundary.

   ..Squitieri/Mosier.. 08/08/2026

   ...Please see www.spc.noaa.gov for graphic product...

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Pittsburgh PA
634 PM EDT Sat Aug 8 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
A Slight Risk of Excessive Rainfall has been added for Monday. 
Otherwise, forecast remains on track with an active weather 
pattern in place through much of the week.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) Another round of showers/storms are possible this 
evening/overnight but should be more scattered in nature. These 
storms could but present a slightly higher wind gust potential.

2) After a break on Sunday, daily shower and thunderstorm chances 
return Monday and remain in the forecast through at least Thursday 
with both the potential for strong/severe storms and heavy rainfall.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1... 
Isolated to scattered thunderstorms are attempting to develop
along a nominal surface dewpoint gradient and marginal upper
support as of 630pm, stretching from central OH into northwest 
PA. Notable mid-level dry air seen via Satellite and ACARS 
soundings have made storm up growth more of a slog. However, 
~25kts effective shear with mlCAPE values above 2000 J/kg are 
allowing a few more to become organized, especially as their 
initial updrafts moisten the near-storm air, and offering 
greater risks for damaging winds with above 1000 J/kg DCAPE 
available areawide. 

For the rest of the evening, damaging wind is likely to be the
primary risk as storms progress east, especially if stronger
cold pools develop to aide in storm clustering. Flash flooding
is not likely due to lower rainfall rates (PWAT is down and
slowly falling) than prior days' values while forward storm 
motion of 25 mph should limit rain duration at a given location.
If any flooding occurs, it will be in areas with poor drainage
or previously experiencing flooding that sees a storm that
better maximizes rainfall rates.

Both threats should lower after 10pm but may not completely end
as elevated buoyancy and shortwave movement maintains varying
storm chances before exiting southeast of the region by early
Sunday morning.

KEY MESSAGE 2... 
Surface and shortwave ridging provide for a brief reprieve from
the daily rounds of storms on Sunday. 

Very broad troughing will remain in place until at least Wednesday 
before a stronger shortwave deepens the trough over the Great Lakes. 
With prevailing W-NW flow and disturbances passing through the upper 
pattern, there will be daily chances for showers and thunderstorms, 
with the potential for more organized convective complexes as hinted 
to in some of the guidance. Precipitable water values remain above-
normal in a climatological sense through this period, and as several 
areas already well saturated, will generally take less
precipitation to pose a flood risk. As such, WPC does have 
portions of the upper Ohio in a Slight Risk (level 2 of 4) for 
excessive rainfall Monday- Wednesday. Think it could be very 
well be possible a Flood Watch is issued at some point during 
this time frame but there remains some run to run spatial 
inconsistency, which will be better resolved in the 12-24 hour 
time scale as the day priors convection may shift where the 
threat is the next day. 

In addition to the flood threat, severe weather chances show an 
uptick as well, particularly earlier in the week according to the 
long-range machine-learning convective guidance. This makes sense, 
as this period shows the best juxtaposition of instability, moderate 
deep-layer shear, and decent low-level flow. Some uncertainty 
remains among the various ensemble members that will be better 
resolved in time.

&&

.AVIATION /22Z SATURDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
VFR favored for the majority of the TAF period with isolated to
locally scattered thunderstorms possible through early Sunday
morning ahead of a nominal surface boundary. The environment
remains conducive to thunderstorm development outside of
excessive dry air aloft, but limited forcing likely will keep
storm coverage low and make terminal impacts more uncertain.
Outside of FKL/DUJ, where storms are closer to impact, keep
thunderstorm chances to PROB30 groups with updated timing based
on where storms initiated this afternoon.

Pending early morning clearing, there is potential for a short
period of IFR cigs/vsbys in lower stratus/fog but confidence in
low in timing and coverage of such restrictions. Any that do
develop will mix out by 15z as diurnal heating scatters out
residual clouds.

Outlook... 
Active weather returns Monday through the later half of the week
with varying rounds of showers and thunderstorms. Timing of
storms for a given day is likely to be of lower confidence and
dependent on upstream storm progression. Most restrictions
during this period will be tied to storm activity and/or morning
fog/stratus resultant of rain plus overnight clearing.

&&

.PBZ WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
PA...None.
OH...None.
WV...None.

&&
